package_info.package_versions: Affected versions as per CVE-2017-8046 (exact versions not specified in the report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2017-8046) that allows attackers to exploit insecure deserialization in the Spring Data REST framework, potentially leading to remote code execution. While not intentionally malicious, the presence of this vulnerability enables malicious exploitation.

execution_context.file_location: Spring Data REST controller (Java class handling HTTP PATCH requests)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes user-supplied HTTP PATCH request bodies using a generic ObjectMapper, allowing attacker-controlled data to be deserialized into arbitrary Java objects, which can lead to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted user input without proper validation or type restrictions is a well-known security risk, as it can allow attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes and trigger malicious code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict deserialization to safe types or sanitize input; the actual behavior allows arbitrary deserialization from user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization is legitimate when used with trusted data sources or with strict type controls and input validation.
key_indicators: Lack of input validation or type restriction
Use of generic ObjectMapper in HTTP request handler

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP PATCH request with malicious serialized data to the vulnerable REST endpoint.
The vulnerable code deserializes the malicious payload, instantiating attacker-specified classes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential remote code execution or further exploitation

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of user-supplied data in HTTP request handlers
Use of generic ObjectMapper or similar deserialization APIs on untrusted input
PATCH/PUT/POST endpoints accepting arbitrary object types
network_indicators: Unusual or malformed PATCH requests to REST endpoints
Serialized Java object payloads in HTTP request bodies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Review REST controllers for deserialization of user-supplied data without type restrictions. Monitor for PATCH requests with serialized object payloads. Use static analysis to flag ObjectMapper.readValue or similar calls on untrusted input. Employ runtime monitoring for deserialization of unexpected types during HTTP request processing.
